summary_html: Reports via **state hotlines** (anonymous or confidential). CAPTA conditions funding on operating intake systems with confidentiality and good-faith protections.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — intake, confidentiality, immunity, and data requirements tied to federal funding

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court of appeals held that a person with reasonable grounds to report suspected child abuse has qualified statutory immunity defeasible only by proof of malice, but reversed and remanded because the immunity ruling did not dispose of the plaintiffs' separate negligent-treatment and consortium claims.
key_cases.relevance: Protects good-faith hotline reports absent proof of malice.
key_cases.quote: Malicious intent must be proved by the plaintiff to defeat the defense of qualified immunity.

key_cases.case_name: Ramsey v. Yavapai Family Advocacy Center
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed summary judgment for the reporter and the forensic interviewers, holding that A.R.S. § 13-3620(J) confers qualified immunity conditioned on the initial reporter's reasonable belief that abuse occurred and that a counselor owes no duty to a third-party alleged abuser.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms that immunity protects the hotline report itself only where the reporter reasonably believed abuse occurred.
key_cases.quote: as the initial reporter of the alleged abuse, Sheets enjoys qualified immunity under the statute only if she "reasonably believe[d]" abuse had occurred

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Ninth Circuit affirmed the denial of qualified immunity, holding that a social worker and a police officer who coerced entry into a home and strip-searched a child during a child-abuse investigation, without a warrant, consent, or exigency, violated clearly established Fourth and Fourteenth Amendment rights.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes that an uncorroborated tip does not create the exigency needed to enter a home without consent.
key_cases.quote: everyone knew that the government could not so enter houses, and White said that principle was well established, in the context of a child abuse investigation

mandatory_reporters: Physicians, physician assistants, optometrists, dentists, osteopathic physicians, chiropractors, podiatrists, behavioral health professionals, nurses, psychologists, counselors and social workers who form the belief while treating a patient — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(1)
Peace officers, child welfare investigators, child safety workers, members of the clergy, priests and Christian Science practitioners — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(2)
The parent, stepparent or guardian of the minor — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(3)
School personnel, including substitute teachers, and domestic violence or sexual assault victim advocates who form the belief in the course of their employment — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(4)
Any other person who has responsibility for the care or treatment of the minor — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(5)
Immediate or next-higher-level supervisors and administrators of a person listed in (A)(1), (2), (4) or (5) — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(6)
Members of a school district governing board or charter school governing body — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(7)
reporting_details: In Arizona a person listed in A.R.S. § 13-3620(A) must report immediately, electronically or by telephone, to a peace officer, to the Department of Child Safety, or — for an Indian minor who resides on an Indian reservation — to a tribal law enforcement or social services agency (A.R.S. § 13-3620(A), (D)).

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: A.R.S. § 8-456 states no penalty; the report must still reach the court 48 hours before a dependency hearing or within 21 days after a dependency petition is filed (A.R.S. § 8-456(F)(3)(b)).
